reviewer_summary.question: Why must a chosen word be processed before choosing what follows it, and what repeated work can each layer’s cache save?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: Choosing blue uses the earlier word’s finished result; processing blue creates its own result, while saved keys and values let it read earlier pieces without preparing them again.

findings.problem: It is unclear whether the earlier finished number was also discarded; retaining it could avoid rebuilding it for the second-layer preparation.

resolution.note: Explicitly compare a kept-K/V route with a replay retaining only text and fixed rules, without earlier working results.

findings.problem: Another complete decimal sequence displaces the opening question and its reason for a second layer.

resolution.note: Motivate the second-layer result as the chooser input. Repeated known operations now appear as parallel source rows per operation; the rule and all operands/results remain visible.

findings.problem: Extra sharing parts sounds like another quantity rather than the already-taught positive part.

resolution.note: Use positive part consistently in narration and labels.
